name: KitaroDB
tagline: Synergex's free embedded key-value store for WinRT, Windows Phone and Win32 apps (2012-2015).
description: KitaroDB was an embedded NoSQL store from Synergex, the company behind the Synergy DBL language and its ISAM engine. It ran in-process on Windows Store (WinRT), Windows Phone 8 and Win32 apps and exposed both a key-value API and 'intrusive key' records whose keys are segments of the stored data, callable from C#, VB, C++, C and HTML5/JavaScript Windows apps. It was a free download and claimed tens of thousands of operations per second on devices. Version 2.0 (May 2013) added Windows Phone 8, and the last NuGet release, 2.3.1, appeared in August 2015. With Microsoft's mobile platforms gone the product disappeared, and kitarodb.com is now a domain for sale.
statusNote: Last release 2.3.1 (Aug 2015); product site gone and domain for sale. Use SQLite, LiteDB or Realm for embedded .NET storage.

pricing.notes: Was a free download; no longer distributed except old NuGet packages.

strengths: Native support for WinRT, Windows Phone 8 and Win32 from one engine
Intrusive-key records allowed multiple keys over stored data
Callable from .NET, C++ and HTML5/JavaScript Windows apps
weaknesses: Discontinued; tied to dead Windows Phone/WinRT platforms
Closed source with no remaining documentation site
useCases: Maintaining old Windows Store or Windows Phone apps that used it
Historical reference for mobile embedded stores
